summary: scrapetools2 fetches, decrypts, and executes Python from a mutable IPNS pointer at runtime
details: The package's downloader.updater() resolves a hardcoded IPNS name (/ipns/k51qzi5uqu5dmh5178x8jzdkz8u3k3qona4zrwlvdr6865it3901l1oe8emjwc) through three IPFS gateways (eu.orbitor.dev, dget.top, ipfs.filebase.io), pulls a tar.gz, Fernet-decrypts its contents using keys shipped in the package's 'versions' file, writes the decrypted Python into modules/*.py, then compile()s and exec()s each module. This update loop is spawned in a background thread that runs every 60 seconds once DBConsumer.startQueue() is called, which is part of the package's advertised API. A separate packer.unpackdata() routine z85-decodes and Fernet-decrypts a bundled 'updates' ciphertext blob using the same shipped keys, feeding the same write-module-and-exec pipeline. The IPNS pointer is mutable and controlled by whoever holds the signing key, so the executed code can be rotated at any time without any change to the published package. The Fernet+z85 layer obfuscates both the shipped payload and the fetched payload, hiding what actually runs from static inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
